description: This donut chart illustrates the task taxonomy for the MMAR benchmark, categorizing deep reasoning tasks across speech, audio, and music into four hierarchical layers based on their conceptual scope. The largest segment is the Perception Layer (40.4%), depicted in dark blue, encompassing subtasks such as Environmental Perception & Reasoning, Counting & Statistics, Music Theory, Correlation Analysis, Temporal Analysis, and Spatial Analysis. The Semantic Layer (41.2%), shown in medium blue, represents the largest portion and includes Content Analysis, Emotion & Intention, and Speaker Analysis. The Cultural Layer (14.1%), in light gray, covers Culture of Speaker, Professional Knowl & Reasoning, and Imagination. The smallest segment is the Signal Layer (4.3%), in very light blue, comprising Audio Difference Analysis, Anomaly Detection, and Acoustic Quality Analysis. Each layer is further subdivided into specific analytical tasks, with percentage labels indicating their proportional contribution to the overall taxonomy. The chart uses color coding and radial segmentation to visually distinguish between layers and their constituent tasks, with no slices exploded or emphasized beyond their proportional size.
